title: Infra GPU fleet capacity, IaC modules, and CI/CD playbook
author: Liam Chen
content:
Summary

This playbook documents the standardized approach for managing Redwood's GPU fleet and capacity lifecycle across cloud accounts and VPCs, the Terraform/IaC module patterns we use to provision GPU infrastructure, and the CI/CD and build pipelines used to test and deploy infra changes. It is an operational reference for on-call, infra engineers, and platform teams responsible for capacity planning, provisioning, and incident response.

Goals and scope

- Ensure predictable capacity for inference workloads with minimal latency regressions.
- Provide repeatable IaC patterns for GPU node pools, subnet/networking, and RBAC across cloud accounts.
- Standardize CI/CD for Terraform modules to catch drift and validate changes before production rollout.
- Provide runbooks for capacity incidents, planned expansions, and postmortem hygiene.

Audience

- Infra and platform engineers
- SREs owning capacity SLOs
- Solutions/Customer engineers coordinating private deployments

Ownership and contacts

- Primary owner: infra/gpu-capacity team (oncall roster in PagerDuty: infra-gpu-capacity)
- Secondary: cloud-accounts and networking team
- PagerDuty escalation: infra-team -> infra-leads -> eng-sre
- Slack channels: #infra-gpu, #cloud-accounts, #oncall-infra

Service-level targets (internal operational objectives)

| Metric | Target | Thresholds (warning / critical) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Node pool availability | 99.95% monthly | 99.9% / 99.5% | Includes control-plane and instance provisioning delays |
| Average GPU utilization (prod) | 55% target | 70% warning / 85% critical | Trigger capacity add when sustained above warning for 6h |
| Queueing latency (inference requests) | p95 < 250ms | 350ms / 500ms | Measured at API gateway route /model-infer |
| Eviction rate (preemptibles/spot) | < 0.5% | 1% / 3% | Track per-region |

Capacity planning and cadence

1. Monthly capacity review (owners: infra/gpu-capacity + eng-sre)
   - Run utilization and projection report for last 30/90/180 days.
   - Forecast growth using 90th percentile of daily growth rate.
   - Determine required reserved instances / committed capacity for next quarter.

2. Triggered scaling (automated + manual):
   - Automated horizontal scaling: autoscaler will add nodes when pending pods > 10 or average GPU util > 65% for 10 minutes.
   - Manual: when forecasting indicates >20% shortage in next 7 days, open capacity request ticket (Jira: INFRA-CAP) and follow provisioning checklist below.

Provisioning checklist (high level)

- Confirm cloud account and quota availability. Use the cloud-accounts dashboard to verify CPU/GPU quota.
- Verify VPC subnet capacity and available IPs in target AZs.
- Confirm security controls: NSGs, private link endpoints, and required SAs with least privilege.
- Create a Terraform change in feature branch using recommended modules.
- Run CI (terraform fmt, validate, plan). Share plan with reviewer.
- Apply to preprod/staging account, smoke test workloads (synthetic traffic at expected QPS).
- Promote to prod using canary rollout (add capacity in one region first).

Terraform/IaC module patterns

We standardize on modular, composable modules stored in the infra-modules repo. Modules must be idempotent, documented, and tested. Key modules:

- vpc-core: core VPC, subnets by AZ, route tables, NATs, flow logs
- network-interfaces: security groups, VPC endpoints, firewall policy bindings
- gpu-node-pool: instance template, node pool autoscaling config, taints/labels, GPU driver installation hooks
- iam-bindings: minimal service accounts, roles, and instance profiles
- monitoring-exports: Prometheus exporters, Cloud Monitoring sinks, logging config

Module usage example (gpu-node-pool)

| Variable | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| name | string | (required) | Node pool logical name |
| region | string | (required) | Cloud region |
| gpu_type | string | "nvidia-a100" | GPU SKU |
| min_size | number | "0" | Min nodes |
| max_size | number | "100" | Max nodes |
| vm_image | string | "r-inference-ubuntu-22" | Base image with drivers |
| preemptible | bool | "false" | Use spot/preemptible instances |

Sample Terraform usage (excerpt):

```hcl
module "gpu_node_pool" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood/infra-modules.git//gpu-node-pool?ref=v1.8.0"
  name   = "prod-a100-pool-us-west1"
  region = "us-west1"
  gpu_type = "nvidia-a100"
  min_size = 2
  max_size = 80
  vm_image = "r-inference-ubuntu-22"
  preemptible = true
}
```

Idempotency and drift detection

- All modules must include output of resource fingerprints for drift detection.
- Run terraform plan in cadence (daily in prod sandbox) and alert on unexpected changes.
- CI job: nightly-terraform-drift-check lists plans for all prod accounts and files JIRA if plan != empty and not gated.

CI/CD and testing strategy for infra changes

Pipeline stages (each change to infra-modules or platform repo):

1. lint + fmt (terraform fmt, tflint)
2. unit tests (terratest for module-level checks; image build tests)
3. plan (terraform plan against a disposable workspace using mocked variables)
4. policy checks (OPA/Conftest: ensure tagging, encryption, private networking rules)
5. integration apply to staging/preprod with automated smoke tests (run a synthetic inference job for 5 minutes)
6. manual approval for prod apply

CI configuration example (summary):

- CI image: hashicorp/terraform:1.4 + terratest runner
- Secrets: stored in Vault, limited-secrets-per-job pattern
- Approval: GitHub CODEOWNERS + required approver from cloud-accounts and infra-gpu-capacity

Build and image promotion for node images

- Use Packer/HashiCorp image pipelines to bake AMIs/container images with GPU drivers and startup hooks.
- Image pipeline stages: build -> test on small instance -> sign -> publish to image registry -> tag in Terraform variables.
- Rollout: image update in node pool follows canary: update 5% nodes, monitor GPU eviction/errors for 30 min, then continue.

Runbooks (operational)

A. High GPU utilization (sustained warning/critical)

1. Verify dashboards: GPU utilization by region, pending pods, node utilization heatmap.
   - PromQL examples: avg_over_time(gpu_utilization_percent[10m]) by (region)
2. Check autoscaler logs and pending pods:
   - kubectl get pods -n model-serving --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o wide
3. If autoscaler failed to scale: check node pool quota and cloud API errors.
   - gcloud compute regions describe --region=us-west1  # (or aws/az cli equivalents)
4. Manual remedial steps:
   - Increase node pool max_size by +20% (terraform change) and apply to staging then prod (follow CI).
   - Alternatively, provision temporary burst pool (preemptible) with short TTL and route low-priority workloads there.
5. Post-incident: record incident in Jira INFRA-INC, update capacity forecast.

B. Node provisioning failures / slow boot

1. Check instance health in cloud console and cloud-init logs from instance (ssh or serial console).
2. If driver module failing, redeploy image build and roll node pool to updated image.
3. If control-plane (K8s) scheduling issues, cordon affected nodes and recreate.

C. Network or routing impacting model traffic

1. Validate VPC flow logs and security group changes.
2. Confirm private-link endpoints and DNS entries are healthy.
3. If cross-account peering issue, escalate to cloud-accounts: include traceroute, VPC peering id, and recent terraform plan.

Pre-approved quick actions (for oncall)

- Provision a temporary preemptible pool up to X GPUs (pre-approved budget cap $X/day).
- Re-route low-priority test traffic to staging endpoints.
- Toggle model routing to lower-cost / smaller model variant for affected routes (via routing policy in model-serving config).

Testing and validation matrix

- Unit: terratest unit tests for each module (target: >90% coverage for logic paths)
- Integration: apply to staging account + run synthetic inference load test (p95 latency < 300ms)
- E2E: smoke tests with sample RLHF traffic where applicable

Operational playbook: add a new cloud account and VPC for GPU workloads

1. Request new cloud account via cloud-accounts process and obtain account id.
2. Assign owner, billing tag, and compliance classification.
3. Provision base VPC using vpc-core module (use approved subnet sizing table).
4. Configure network-interfaces module: NSGs, private endpoints (artifact registry, secrets manager), and flow logs.
5. Create gpu-node-pool module in test account, deploy one small node pool.
6. Run image smoke test and synthetic inference tests.
7. Add to monitoring and alerting (dashboards, SLOs), add to capacity reports.

Subnet sizing reference

| Environment | AZs | /24 subnets per AZ recommended | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| prod | 3 | /24 | Reserve 50% for service IPs and future growth |
| staging | 2 | /24 | Smaller scale |
| sandbox | 1 | /25 | Short-lived test environments |

CI/CD runbook snippets and useful commands

- Local terraform plan against prod-account workspace (use terragrunt wrapper):

```bash
export TF_WORKSPACE=prod-us-west1
terragrunt plan --terragrunt-working-dir=./envs/prod/us-west1 -out=tfplan.binary
terragrunt show -json tfplan.binary > plan.json
```

- Apply with approval: create PR with plan, request approvers, then run apply from CI agent with least-privilege token.

- Nightly drift check job (example):

```bash
for env in prod-us-west1 prod-eu1; do
  terragrunt plan --terragrunt-working-dir=./envs/$env -detailed-exitcode || true
done
```

Postmortem and continuous improvement

- Every capacity incident must follow the postmortem template: timeline, impact, root cause, remediation, and follow-up action with owner and due date.
- Maintain a rolling action queue for capacity optimizations (batching, caching, model routing changes).

References and related pages

- infra-modules repo: git@github.com:redwood/infra-modules
- GPU capacity dashboards: Grafana > Infra > GPU Fleet
- Cloud account onboarding: confluence:cloud-accounts/onboarding-playbook
- Image baking pipeline: confluence:eng-infra/images-and-baking

Appendix: quick checklist for incident handoff

- Attach: relevant graphs (utilization, queue length), terraform plan for recent changes, cloud provider event logs, and temp credentials used.
- Assign action owner and target due date for each follow-up.

If you find gaps in this playbook or need a new checklist (e.g., for new GPU SKUs or private deployments), open a PR against this page and notify the reviewers listed at the top.
